subject: Different DICs depending on the approximation and integration methods?

messages.author: cd79aec8f4be0778
messages.subject: Different DICs depending on the approximation and integration methods?
parts:
Dear all,

 

I'm doing some poisson (without offset) spatial models (specifically a "bym" model) introducing only one covariate in each one (bivariate models). I'm analyzing 1668 small areas.

 

I write in this forum because I don't understand why I obtain higher DIC, p.eff and deviance with the Laplace approximation and the GRID method with respect to the default approximation and integration methods (simplified Laplace and CCD). More or less, with the first options (Laplace and GRID) I obtain DICs values around 3400 and p.eff around 971, while these values are 2807 and 697 with the second approach (simplified and CCD).

 

I'm confused because I thought that changing approximation and integration method should not change a lot DIC and GRID values. Finally, I have to mention that I have a lot of zeros (75%) in my dependent variable. Could these zeros produce this instable DIC and p.eff?

 

Thank you very much,

 

Marc

the case. I guess that the posterior is almost singular and this
creates problems in the sense that even small changes can make a huge
impact. If you try to make it more stable it would be better.
